phase_name: Read Surfaces — Evidence View, Work Pages & Catalogue Integration

Licence gate urgency.question: When does the reuse_ok gate land?
Licence gate urgency.answer: Neither — owner ruling: the works are public and shown deliberately. Not an exposure, not a hotfix.
options_presented: Hotfix now, ahead of the phase

Licence gate urgency.question: What should a reader see for a licence-gated work?
Licence gate urgency.answer: Moot — 'if I publish it, it means I decide it's ok'.

Licence gate urgency.question: JA: public text, no reuse_ok flag. Which reading governs?
Licence gate urgency.answer: Set the flag deliberately for the 21 JA works.
options_presented: Fail closed — absent is not yes

Licence gate urgency.question: What should the code actually enforce?
Licence gate urgency.answer: NO GATE — render whatever is staged. Staging a work in the reference corpus IS the decision. Concern raised (a new work renders with nobody deciding) and reaffirmed by owner.
options_presented: Owner-set flag, fail closed on absent
No gate — render whatever is staged

Licence gate urgency.question: Does the ruling cover the 46 unclear and 1 noncommercial_only?
Licence gate urgency.answer: Everything currently rendering. One ruling, across the board.

SC1 drift fail-close.question: How should the excerpt detect that the page text has moved on?
SC1 drift fail-close.answer: Re-bake is the guarantee. No render-time detector. FINDING: the excerpt table stores the text itself (frag_before/span/after) plus text_layer but NO page-text hash or snapshot id, so the shipped view never applies offsets to live text and cannot have the offset bug SC1 was written against; the real risk is undetectable staleness.
options_presented: Stamp a snapshot hash, compare at render

SC1 drift fail-close.question: Reader switches the version selector to a source the excerpt wasn't cut from. Then what?
SC1 drift fail-close.answer: Ignore - the identification is about the manuscript, not about one transcription of it. Excerpt stands regardless of selected source.
options_presented: Label which layer it came from
Ignore - the match is about the manuscript

SC1 drift fail-close.question: Rewrite SC1 to the shipped architecture, or keep it as the target?
SC1 drift fail-close.answer: Rewrite SC1 to the real mechanism, so the criterion describes something verifiable. Consequence: SC1's remaining work collapses to a re-specification plus a re-bake discipline note.
options_presented: Rewrite SC1 to the real mechanism
Keep SC1, mark it partially met

/work/{id} page shape.question: Focused witness map, or a browse surface in its own right?
/work/{id} page shape.answer: Witness map PLUS work context - the unit-grouped carrier list with band+library filters, plus a header giving work identity (title, author, witness count, manuscript count) so the page is worth landing on from outside. FINDING: the service is already built (get_work_witnesses_async with anchor_sys_id=None; build_work_expansion_count_sql for the real total); the page is the missing part, not the query.

/work/{id} page shape.question: Does the findings page facet already satisfy WORK-02's 'findable by neutral title'?
/work/{id} page shape.answer: YES - mark WORK-02 met by the /computed-identifications domain/author/work cascade (web/pages/findings.py) and record where. This phase only adds the links into /work/{id}. Removes the work-browse chunk from the phase.
options_presented: Yes - mark it met, note where
Partly - the title normalization is still owed
No - a work index is still wanted

/work/{id} page shape.question: Where do links to /work/{id} come from?
/work/{id} page shape.answer: Connections panel work titles, findings page rows, and catalog-browse rows. Atlas EXCLUDED (its explorer is unbuilt, Phase 139b - nothing to link from yet).
